title: Bomb threat
about: Helps the person who takes a bomb threat by phone in New Zealand: what to ask and write down during the call, who to tell, and what to write after it. Also covers a threat by email or social media, and a suspicious item someone finds. It keeps the times Police will want.

sources.name: NZ Police, "Bomb threat checklist" card (POL 940, printed 11/02) (main source)
NZ Police, web page "Suspicious mail and bomb threats"
NZ Police, web page "How you can help" (Protecting crowded places from attack)
ANZCTC, "Improvised Explosive Device (IED) Guidelines for Crowded Places" (Commonwealth of Australia 2023), Appendix B

warning: In New Zealand call 111. Best used by a colleague beside the person on the phone. The NZ card is old (11/02); the Australian checklist is shown where it adds or differs, and says 000.
audience: Anyone in a New Zealand workplace who answers the phone, and the colleague helping them
version: NZ Police 'Bomb threat checklist' card (POL 940, printed '11/02', no other date; no newer NZ version found); NZ Police web pages 'Suspicious mail and bomb threats' and 'How you can help' (no dates shown, footer 2026); ANZCTC 'Improvised Explosive Device (IED) Guidelines for Crowded Places' (Commonwealth of Australia 2023, Appendix B Telephoned bomb threat checklist); all read 20 Nov 2026

steps.title: Search or evacuate? Not your call alone

lines.text: The app does not decide. In New Zealand the employer decides whether to search or evacuate.

quotes.text: If a bomb threat is received, it is the responsibility of employers to decide whether a search or evacuation will be conducted.

lines.text: The Australian guide: the incident or security manager decides, with Police if possible. It can be total or partial.

quotes.text: Planning and initiating evacuation should be the responsibility of the incident/security manager and, if possible, made in consultation with police and other emergency services.
The decision to initiate a total or partial evacuation may be determined by several factors

lines.text: Things it says to weigh: the nature of the threat, the chance of panic, and the impact on the business of a total evacuation.

quotes.text: the nature of the threat
the potential to cause panic
potential business impacts from total evacuation

lines.text: It says to treat every threat as real until shown otherwise.

quotes.text: Generally speaking, all threats should be deemed credible until proven otherwise.

lines.text: It also lists four questions (is the threat non-specific? do you know the caller? has specific detail been given? is it credible?) and three responses (occupant inspection, supervisory inspection, support a Police search). How the answers lead to a response was in a chart that could not be read, so the app does not link them.

ask.question: What did the employer or incident manager decide?

lines.text: Keep this app with you. Do what the employer, the incident manager or Police tell you.
The guidelines do not say what to do while waiting. Follow your workplace plan.
Evacuation started
Use your workplace's evacuation plan. The guidelines give no distance for a phone threat.
Australian guide: think about secondary devices at assembly points, and keep them clear.

quotes.text: including consideration of secondary devices at assembly points and procedures to ensure these are kept clear

lines.text: Australian guide: be aware that secondary explosions may occur at or near the original blast site, especially as rescue personnel arrive.

quotes.text: Be aware that secondary explosions may occur at or near the original blast site, especially as rescue personnel arrive.

lines.text: Partial evacuation started
The Australian guide gives an example: when a suspicious item is small and thought to be in one place.

quotes.text: the plan may include considerations for total evacuation or partial evacuation, for example, if the suspicious item is small and thought to be confined to one location.

quotes.text: If a threat is communicated, it may be necessary to inspect the venue or facility.

lines.text: Look for anything Hidden, Obviously suspicious or not Typical of the place (Australian guide).
